These forward-looking statements include all matters that are not historical facts. By their nature, forward-looking statements involve risks and uncertainties because they relate to events, and depend on circumstances, that may or may not occur in the future. As a result, actual events may differ materially from those expressed in, or suggested by, the forward-looking statements. Any forward-looking statement made by Turning Point Brands, Inc. (&#8220;TPB&#8221;), in this Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q speaks only as of the date hereof. New risks and uncertainties come up from time to time, and it is impossible for TPB to predict these events or how they may affect it. TPB has no obligation, and does not intend, to update any forward-looking statements after the date hereof, except as required by federal securities laws.    <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">1.</em> Business and Basis of Presentation</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>Description of Business</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">Turning Point Brands, Inc., including its subsidiaries (collectively referred to herein as the &#8220;Company,&#8221; &#8220;we,&#8221; &#8220;our,&#8221; or &#8220;us&#8221;), is a leading manufacturer, marketer and distributor of branded consumer products. The Company sells a wide range of products to adult consumers consisting of staple products with its iconic brands Zig-Zag&#174; and Stoker&#8217;s&#174; and its next generation products to fulfill evolving consumer preferences. The Company's segments are led by its core proprietary and iconic brands: Zig-Zag&#174; and Stoker&#8217;s&#174; along with FRE&#174;, Beech-Nut&#174; and Trophy&#174;. The Company&#8217;s products are available in more than <ix:nonFraction id="c145316217" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:NumberOfStores" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">220,000</ix:nonFraction> retail outlets in North America. The Company operates <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145316218">two</span> segments, Zig-Zag products and Stoker&#8217;s products.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>Basis of Presentation</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The accompanying unaudited, interim, consolidated financial statements have been prepared in accordance with the accounting practices described in the Company&#8217;s audited, consolidated financial statements as of and for the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>. In the opinion of management, the unaudited, interim, consolidated financial statements included herein contain all adjustments necessary to present fairly the financial position, results of operations, and cash flows of the Company for the periods presented. Such adjustments, other than nonrecurring adjustments separately disclosed, are of a normal and recurring nature. The operating results for interim periods are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> necessarily indicative of results to be expected for a full year or future interim periods. The unaudited, interim, consolidated financial statements should be read in conjunction with the Company&#8217;s audited, consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes as of and for the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>. The accompanying interim, consolidated financial statements are presented in accordance with the rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission (the &#8220;SEC&#8221;) and, accordingly, do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> include all the disclosures required by generally accepted accounting principles in the United States (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;) with respect to annual financial statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Certain prior year amounts have been reclassified to conform to the current year&#8217;s presentation. The changes did&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;have an impact on the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial position, results of operations, or cash flows in any of the periods presented.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:SignificantAccountingPoliciesTextBlock" id="c3187148" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">2.</em> Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>Consolidation</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The consolidated financial statements include the accounts of the Company, its subsidiaries, all of which are wholly-owned, and variable interest entities (&#8220;VIEs&#8221;) for which the Company is considered to have a controlling interest based on the voting interest entity model or the variable interest entity model. All significant intercompany transactions have been eliminated.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">U.S. GAAP requires the Company to identify entities for which control is achieved through means other than voting rights and to determine whether the Company is the primary beneficiary of VIEs. A VIE is broadly defined as an entity with&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">one</em>&#160;or more of the following characteristics: (a) the total equity investment at risk is insufficient to finance the entity&#8217;s activities without additional subordinated financial support; (b) as a group, the holders of the equity investment at risk lack (i) the ability to make decisions about the entity&#8217;s activities through voting or similar rights, (ii) the obligation to absorb the expected losses of the entity, or (iii) the right to receive the expected residual returns of the entity; and (c) the equity investors have voting rights that are&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;proportional to their economic interests, and substantially all of the entity&#8217;s activities either involve, or are conducted on behalf of, an investor that has disproportionately few voting rights. The Company consolidates its investment in&#160;a VIE when it determines that it is the VIE&#8217;s primary beneficiary. The Company&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may&#160;</em>change its original assessment of a VIE upon subsequent events such as the modification of contractual arrangements that affects the characteristics or adequacy of the entity&#8217;s equity investments at risk and the disposition of all or a portion of an interest held by the primary beneficiary.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <ix:exclude>

       <a href="#toc" style="font-weight: initial; font-style: initial; font-variant: initial; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Table of Contents</a>

   </ix:exclude>
   <ix:exclude>&#160;</ix:exclude>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The primary beneficiary of a VIE is the entity that has both: (i) the power to direct the activities of the VIE that most significantly impact the entity&#8217;s economic performance; and (ii) the obligation to absorb losses or the right to receive benefits of the VIE that could be significant to the entity. The Company performs this analysis on an ongoing basis.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">The Company determines whether an entity is a VIE at the inception of its variable interest in the entity and upon the occurrence of certain reconsideration events.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">Management of the Company has determined that Turning Point Brands Canada and ALP Supply Co, LLC (&#8220;ALP&#8221;) are VIEs for which the Company is required to consolidate and determined that the distribution business acquired by General Wireless Operations, Inc. ("GWO") (refer to Note <em style="font: inherit;">7,</em> "Other Assets") is a VIE for which the Company is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> required to consolidate. The Company has a <ix:nonFraction id="c145316242" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_OwnershipAxis-TurningPointBrandsCanadaMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:VariableInterestEntityOwnershipPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">65</ix:nonFraction>% financial interest in the equity of Turning Point Brands Canada, provides additional subordinated financing and has a distribution agreement for the sale of the Company&#8217;s products that makes up a significant portion of Turning Point Brands Canada&#8217;s business activities. The Company has a <ix:nonFraction id="c145316246" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_OwnershipAxis-AlpSupplyCoLlcMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:VariableInterestEntityOwnershipPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">50</ix:nonFraction>% equity interest in ALP, provides additional financing, has a supply agreement to be the exclusive provider of product and is the primary beneficiary due to the power the Company has over the activities that most significantly impact the economic performance, and the right to receive benefits and the obligation to absorb losses. RSH Holding Trust ("RSH Trust"), which was established by the Company and is managed by an independent trustee that votes our interest in GWO in accordance with GWO's board's recommendations, holds a <ix:nonFraction id="c145316249" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_OwnershipAxis-GeneralWirelessOperationsIncMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:VariableInterestEntityOwnershipPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">49</ix:nonFraction>% indirect interest in the distribution business through its interests in GWO&#160;and, the Company, through Turning Point Brands Canada, has a variable interest through a purchase option to acquire the equity interests of GWO's distribution business. However, the Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have the ability to direct the activities that impact the performance of the business. GWO is controlled by Standard General, L.P. Based on the foregoing, management believes in its judgement that the distribution business is a VIE for which the Company is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> required to consolidate. See Note <em style="font: inherit;">7</em>&#160;"Other Assets" for further discussion of the acquisition of the distribution business by GWO. and the terms of the option on its equity interests. Turning Point Brands Canada charged a fee to the distribution business in <em style="font: inherit;">2025.</em> The agreement was terminated in the <em style="font: inherit;">fourth</em> quarter of <em style="font: inherit;">2025.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">Subsequent to the acquisition of the distribution business by GWO, the Company determined that the GWO equity method investment is a VIE of which we are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> the primary beneficiary. We considered the Company&#8217;s interest at risk due to a lack of power, through voting rights, to direct the activities that most significantly impact GWO's economic performance. Standard General, L.P&#8217;s voting rights are conveyed through an equity interest that is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> considered at risk. Based on the foregoing, management believes in its judgement that GWO is a VIE for which the Company is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> required to consolidate.</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>Revenue Recognition</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company recognizes revenues in accordance with Accounting Standards Codification (&#8220;ASC&#8221;) <em style="font: inherit;">606,</em> Revenue from Contracts with Customers, which includes excise taxes and shipping and handling charges billed to customers, net of cash discounts for prompt payment, sales returns and incentives, upon delivery of goods to the customer &#8211; at which time the Company&#8217;s performance obligation is satisfied - at an amount that the Company expects to be entitled to in exchange for those goods in accordance with the <em style="font: inherit;">five</em>-step analysis outlined in ASC <em style="font: inherit;">606:</em> (i) identify the contract with the customer, (ii) identify the performance obligations in the contract, (iii) determine the transaction price, (iv) allocate the transaction price to the performance obligations, and (v) recognize revenue when (or as) performance obligations are satisfied. The Company includes in its transaction price excise taxes on smokeless tobacco, cigars or other nicotine products billed to customers, and excludes sales taxes and value-added taxes imposed at the time of sale.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company records an allowance for sales returns, based principally on historical volume and return rates, which is included in accrued liabilities on the consolidated balance sheets. The Company records sales incentives, which consist of consumer incentives and trade promotion activities, as a reduction in revenues (a portion of which is based on amounts estimated to be due to wholesalers, retailers and consumers at the end of the period) based principally on historical volume and utilization rates. Expected payments for sales incentives are included in accrued liabilities on the consolidated balance sheets.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">A further requirement of ASC <em style="font: inherit;">606</em> is for entities to disaggregate revenue recognized from contracts with customers into categories that depict how the nature, amount, timing&#160;and uncertainty of revenue and cash flows are affected by economic factors. The Company&#8217;s management views business performance through segments that closely resemble the performance of major product lines. Thus, the primary and most useful disaggregation of the Company&#8217;s contract revenue for decision making purposes is the disaggregation by segment which can be found in Note <em style="font: inherit;">14,</em> &#8220;Segment Information&#8221;.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>Shipping Costs</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company records shipping costs incurred as a component of selling, general&#160;and administrative expenses. Shipping costs incurred were approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c145316271" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="tpb:ShippingCosts" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">8.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c145316272" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="tpb:ShippingCosts" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">7.4</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million for the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ending <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>Inventories</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Inventories are stated at the lower of cost or net realizable value using the <em style="font: inherit;">first</em>-in, <em style="font: inherit;">first</em>-out method. Leaf tobacco is presented in current assets in accordance with standard industry practice, notwithstanding the fact that such tobacco&#160;is&#160;carried longer than <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> year for the purpose of curing.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Fair Value</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">U.S. GAAP establishes a framework for measuring fair value. That framework provides a fair value hierarchy that prioritizes the inputs to valuation techniques used to measure fair value. The hierarchy gives the highest priority to unadjusted quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities (Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em>) and the lowest priority to unobservable inputs (Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em>).</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> levels of the fair value hierarchy under U.S. GAAP are described below:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> &#8211;&#160;Inputs to the valuation methodology are unadjusted quoted prices for identical assets or liabilities in active markets at the measurement date.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> &#8211;&#160;Inputs to the valuation methodology include quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities in active markets;&#160;quoted prices for identical or similar assets or liabilities in inactive markets;&#160;inputs other than quoted prices that are observable for the asset or liability;&#160;and inputs that are derived principally from or corroborated by observable market data by correlation or other means.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> &#8211;&#160;Unobservable inputs that reflect management&#8217;s best estimate of what market participants would use in pricing the asset or liability at the measurement date.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"><i style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">Derivative Instruments</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company enters into foreign currency forward contracts to hedge a portion of its exposure to changes in foreign currency exchange rates on inventory purchase commitments. The Company accounts for its forward contracts under the provisions of ASC <em style="font: inherit;">815,</em> Derivatives and Hedging. Under the Company&#8217;s policy, the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>hedge up to <ix:nonFraction id="c145316287" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" unitRef="Pure" name="tpb:PercentageOfAnticipatedPurchasesOfInventoryThatMayBeHedged" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="0">100</ix:nonFraction>% of its anticipated purchases of inventory in the denominated invoice currency over a forward period <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> to exceed <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145316289">twelve</span> months. The Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>also, from time to time, hedge up to <ix:nonFraction id="c145316290" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" unitRef="Pure" name="tpb:PercentageOfNonInventoryPurchasesThatMayBeHedged" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="0">100</ix:nonFraction>% of its non-inventory purchases (e.g., production equipment) in the denominated invoice currency. Forward contracts that qualify as hedges are adjusted to their fair value through other comprehensive income as determined by market prices on the measurement date, except any hedge ineffectiveness which is recognized currently in income. Gains and losses on these forward contracts are reclassified from other comprehensive income into inventory as the related inventories are received and are transferred to net income as inventory is sold. Changes in fair value of any contracts that do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> qualify for hedge accounting or are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> designated as hedges are recognized currently in income.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>Risks and Uncertainties</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Manufacturers and sellers of tobacco products are subject to regulation at the federal, state,&#160;and local levels. Such regulations include, among others, labeling requirements, limitations on advertising, and prohibition of sales to minors. The tobacco industry is likely to continue to be heavily regulated. There can be&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">no</em>&#160;assurance as to the ultimate content, timing, or effect of any regulation of tobacco products by any federal, state, or local legislative or regulatory body, nor can there be any assurance that any such legislation or regulation would&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;have a material adverse effect on the Company&#8217;s financial position, results of operations&#160;or cash flows. In a number of states targeted flavor bans have been proposed or enacted legislatively or by the administrative process. Depending on the number and location of such bans, that legislation or regulation could have a material adverse effect on the Company&#8217;s financial position, results of operations, or cash flows.&#160;The U.S. Food and Drug Administration&#160;(&#8220;FDA&#8221;) continues to consider various restrictive regulations around our products, including targeted flavor bans; however, the details, timing&#160;and ultimate implementation of such measures remain unclear.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The tobacco industry has experienced, and is experiencing, significant product liability litigation. Most tobacco liability lawsuits have been brought against manufacturers and sellers of cigarettes for injuries allegedly caused by smoking or exposure to smoke. However, several lawsuits have been brought against manufacturers and sellers of smokeless products for injuries to health allegedly caused by use of smokeless products. Typically, such claims assert that use of smokeless products is addictive and causes oral cancer.&#160;There can be&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">no</em>&#160;assurance the Company will&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;sustain losses in connection with such lawsuits and that such losses will&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;have a material adverse effect on the Company&#8217;s financial position, results of operations, or cash flows.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="tpb:MasterSettlementAgreementMsaPolicyTextBlock" id="c145327311" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Master Settlement Agreement (MSA)</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Pursuant to the Master Settlement Agreement (the &#8220;MSA&#8221;) entered into in <em style="font: inherit;"> November 1998 </em>by most states (represented by their attorneys general acting through the National Association of Attorneys General) and subsequent states&#8217; statutes, a &#8220;cigarette manufacturer&#8221; (which is defined to include a manufacturer of make-your-own (&#8220;MYO&#8221;) cigarette tobacco) has the option of either becoming a signatory to the MSA or opening, funding&#160;and maintaining an escrow account to have funds available for certain potential tobacco-related liabilities with sub-accounts on behalf of each settling state. Such companies are entitled to direct the investment of the escrowed funds and withdraw any appreciation but cannot withdraw the principal for <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145316298">twenty-five</span> years from the year of each annual deposit, except to withdraw funds deposited pursuant to an individual state&#8217;s escrow statute to pay a final judgement to that state&#8217;s plaintiffs in the event of such a final judgement against the Company. The Company chose to open and fund an escrow account as its method of compliance. It is the Company&#8217;s policy to record amounts on deposit in the escrow account for prior years as a non-current asset.&#160;The Company has begun to receive deposits back from participating&#160;states commencing with the deposits from <em style="font: inherit;">1999.</em> At <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, the Company had on deposit approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c145316300" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DepositAssets" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">32.0</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c145316301" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DepositAssets" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">32.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively, the fair values of which were approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c145316302" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="tpb:DepositAssetsFairValueDisclosure" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">29.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c145316303" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="tpb:DepositAssetsFairValueDisclosure" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">29.9</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively. The Company discontinued its generic category of MYO in <em style="font: inherit;">2019</em> and its&#160;Zig-Zag&#160;branded MYO cigarette smoking tobacco in <em style="font: inherit;">2017.</em> Thus, without a change in MSA legislation, the Company has <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> remaining product lines covered by the MSA and will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be required to make future escrow deposits.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">The Company has chosen to invest a portion of the MSA escrow, from time to time, in U.S. Government securities including Treasury inflation-protected securities, Treasury notes&#160;and Treasury bonds. These investments are classified as available-for-sale and carried at fair value. Realized losses are prohibited under the MSA; thus, any investment with an unrealized loss position will be held until the value is recovered, or until maturity.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c145327312" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>Recent Accounting Pronouncement</i>s</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Issued but <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> yet adopted</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">In&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> November 2024,&#160;</em>the FASB issued guidance requiring reporting entities to disclose in the notes to the financial statements, specified information about certain categories of expenses including purchases of inventory, employee compensation, depreciation and amortization for each caption&#160;on the income statement where such expenses are included.&#160;This guidance will be effective for the Company beginning with its fiscal&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2027</em>&#160;annual financial statements and interim periods thereafter. Early adoption is permitted, in addition to either prospective or retrospective application. The Company is currently assessing the impact and extent to which this guidance will affect its disclosures.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2025, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025&#8209;12,</em> which&#160;makes targeted technical corrections and clarifications to several topics in the Codification, including diluted EPS, leases, and transfers of receivables. The guidance is effective for annual periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026, </em>and interim periods within those annual periods. The Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expect adoption to have a material impact on its consolidated financial statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> September 2025, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025&#8209;06,</em> which updates the accounting guidance for internal&#8209;use software by eliminating the traditional development stage model and requiring capitalization of costs when funding is authorized and completion is probable, unless significant uncertainties exist. The standard is effective for annual reporting periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2027, </em>with early adoption permitted. The Company is currently evaluating the impact of adoption on its consolidated financial statements and disclosures.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">3.</em> Fair Value of Financial Instruments</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The estimated fair value amounts have been determined by the Company using the methods and assumptions described below. However, considerable judgment is required to interpret market data to develop estimates of fair value. Accordingly, the estimates presented herein are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> necessarily indicative of the amounts the Company could realize in a current market exchange. The use of different market assumptions and/or estimation methodologies <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>have a material effect on the estimated fair value amounts.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>Cash and Cash Equivalents</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Cash and cash equivalents are, by definition, short-term. Thus, the carrying amount is a reasonable estimate of fair value.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>Accounts Receivable</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The fair value of accounts receivable approximates their carrying value due to their short-term nature.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>Long-Term Debt</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company's <em style="font: inherit;">2032</em> Notes bear interest at a rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c145316439" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-Notes2032Member" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="5">7.625</ix:nonFraction>% per year. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, the fair value approximated $<ix:nonFraction id="c145316440" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-Notes2032Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFairValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">305.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, with a carrying value of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145316441" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-Notes2032Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentCarryingAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-8">300.0</ix:nonFraction> million. As of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, the fair value approximated $<ix:nonFraction id="c145316442" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-Notes2032Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFairValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">313.8</ix:nonFraction> million, with a carrying value of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145316443" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-Notes2032Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentCarryingAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-8">300.0</ix:nonFraction> million.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">See Note <em style="font: inherit;">9,</em> &#8220;Notes Payable and Long-Term Debt&#8221;, for further information regarding the Company&#8217;s long-term debt.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">The components of inventories are as follows:</p>

The leaf tobacco inventory is covered by the Company&#8217;s stock throughput insurance policy and the Company believes the inventory loss is probable of being fully recovered under the policy.&#160;As a result, the Company recorded a $<ix:nonFraction id="c145316450" contextRef="i_2023-12-31_PublicUtilitiesInventoryAxis-LeafTobaccoInventoryMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InsuranceSettlementsReceivableCurrent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">15.2</ix:nonFraction> million insurance recovery receivable which is included in Other current assets on the consolidated balance sheets.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>Non-Marketable Equity Investments and Option Agreements</i></p>

The Company performs a qualitative assessment on a quarterly basis to determine if the fair value of the Old Pal investment could be less than the amortized cost basis. In addition, the Company utilizes a&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party&#160;to perform a quantitative assessment to determine fair value using a Monte Carlo simulation (Level&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">3</em>) when indicated, and at least bi-annually. Based upon its quantitative fair value assessment, the Company determined the fair value of Old Pal to be $<ix:nonFraction id="c145316545" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_FairValueByFairValueHierarchyLevelAxis-FairValueInputsLevel3Member_ScheduleOfEquityMethodInvestmentEquityMethodInvesteeNameAxis-OldPalHoldingCompanyLlcMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InvestmentsFairValueDisclosure" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">6.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and recorded an allowance for credit losses of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145316546" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_ScheduleOfEquityMethodInvestmentEquityMethodInvesteeNameAxis-OldPalHoldingCompanyLlcMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableAllowanceForCreditLosses" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.9</ix:nonFraction> in <em style="font: inherit;"> June 2025. </em>The Company has recorded an accrued interest receivable of&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c145316547" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_ScheduleOfEquityMethodInvestmentEquityMethodInvesteeNameAxis-OldPalHoldingCompanyLlcMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InterestReceivableCurrent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million&#160;and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c145316548" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_ScheduleOfEquityMethodInvestmentEquityMethodInvesteeNameAxis-OldPalHoldingCompanyLlcMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InterestReceivableCurrent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million&#160;at <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>,&#160;respectively, in Other current assets on its Consolidated Balance Sheets.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>Captive Investments - Available-for-Sale Marketable Securities</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2023, </em>the Company formed a captive insurance company, Interchange, IC, incorporated in the District of Columbia, to write a portion of its insurance coverage, including with respect to general product, and officer and director liability coverages under deductible reinsurance policies. Interchange, IC is a fully licensed captive insurance company holding a certificate of authority from the District of Columbia Department of Insurance, Securities and Banking. Interchange, IC is consolidated in the Company&#8217;s financial statements. Subsequent to <em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2025, </em>Interchange IC received approval from the District of Columbia Department of Insurance, Securities and Banking to operate as a group captive. On <em style="font: inherit;"> July 14, 2025, </em>a <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party investor subscribed $<ix:nonFraction id="c145316552" contextRef="d_2025-07-14_2025-07-14_ScheduleOfEquityMethodInvestmentEquityMethodInvesteeNameAxis-CanadianAmericanStandardHempMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ConsolidationLessThanWhollyOwnedSubsidiaryParentOwnershipInterestChangesSaleOfInterestByParent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">11.0</ix:nonFraction> million for an interest in Interchange IC&#8217;s parent company, which contributed the investment to Interchange IC. Insurance reserves were $<ix:nonFraction id="c145316553" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_ScheduleOfEquityMethodInvestmentEquityMethodInvesteeNameAxis-CanadianAmericanStandardHempMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:SelfInsuranceReserve" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">0.0</ix:nonFraction> million as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and $<ix:nonFraction id="c145316554" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_ScheduleOfEquityMethodInvestmentEquityMethodInvesteeNameAxis-CanadianAmericanStandardHempMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:SelfInsuranceReserve" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.4</ix:nonFraction> million as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025. </em>As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026, </em><em style="font: inherit;">no</em> policy has been underwritten for the benefit of the <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party investor.&#160;The group captive will write policies for both companies. The Company will continue to control and consolidate the entity.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The investments held within the captive are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> available for operating activities and are carried at fair value on the consolidated balance sheet. They consist of money market, stocks, corporate bonds, government securities and real estate investment trusts. The Company believes any investments held with gross unrealized losses to be temporary and <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> the result of credit risk.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;"><i><em style="font: inherit;">2032</em> Notes</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;">On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> February 19, 2025,&#160;</em>the Company entered into an indenture relating to the issuance and sale of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145316681" contextRef="i_2025-02-19_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2032SeniorSecuredNotesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-8">300.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million aggregate principal amount of its&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c145316682" contextRef="i_2025-02-19_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2032SeniorSecuredNotesMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="5">7.625</ix:nonFraction>% Senior Secured Notes due&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2032</em>&#160;(the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2032</em>&#160;Notes&#8221;), by and among the Company, the guarantors party thereto and GLAS Trust Company LLC, as trustee and notes collateral agent. The <em style="font: inherit;">2032</em> Notes incur interest at a rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c145316686" contextRef="i_2025-02-19_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2032SeniorSecuredNotesMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="5">7.625</ix:nonFraction>%, payable semi-annually in arrears on <em style="font: inherit;"> March 15 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> September 15 </em>of each year, commencing on <em style="font: inherit;"> September 15, 2025.&#160;</em>Proceeds from the offering were approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c145316687" contextRef="d_2025-02-19_2025-02-19_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2032SeniorSecuredNotesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromIssuanceOfLongTermDebt" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">293.0</ix:nonFraction> million and were used to redeem our <ix:nonFraction id="c145316688" contextRef="i_2021-02-11_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2032SeniorSecuredNotesMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="5">5.625</ix:nonFraction>% senior secured notes due <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> issued on <em style="font: inherit;"> February 11, 2021&#160;</em>and for general corporate purposes.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;">The <em style="font: inherit;">2032</em> Notes are fully and unconditionally guaranteed on a senior secured basis, jointly and severally, by certain existing and future wholly-owned domestic subsidiaries&#160;of the Company (collectively, the &#8220;Guarantors&#8221; as defined in the indenture governing the <em style="font: inherit;">2032</em> Notes or the <em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2032</em> Notes Indenture&#8221;).&#160;The&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2032</em>&#160;Notes and the related guarantees are secured by&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">first</em>-priority liens on substantially all of the existing and future assets of the Company and the Guarantors that do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> secure the <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em> ABL Facility (as defined below), subject to certain exceptions. The <em style="font: inherit;">2032</em> Notes Indenture contains covenants that, among other things, restrict the ability of the Company and its restricted subsidiaries to: (i) grant or incur liens; (ii) incur, assume or guarantee additional indebtedness; (iii) sell or otherwise dispose of assets, including capital stock of subsidiaries; (iv) make certain investments; (v) pay dividends, make distributions or redeem or repurchase capital stock; (vi) engage in certain transactions with affiliates; and (vii) consolidate or merge with or into, or sell substantially all of our assets to another entity. These covenants are subject to several limitations and exceptions set forth in the <em style="font: inherit;">2032</em> Notes Indenture. For instance, the Company is generally permitted to make restricted payments, including the payment of dividends to shareholders, provided that, at the time of payment, or as a result of payment, the Company is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> in default on its covenants; however, there are earnings and market capitalization requirements that if <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> met could limit the aggregate amount of quarterly dividends payable during a fiscal year. The <em style="font: inherit;">2032</em> Notes Indenture provides for customary events of default. The Company was in compliance with all covenants under the <em style="font: inherit;">2032</em> Notes as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;">The Company incurred debt issuance costs attributable to the <em style="font: inherit;">2032</em>&#160;Notes of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145316705" contextRef="i_2025-02-19_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2032SeniorSecuredNotesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredFinanceCostsGross" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">7.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million which are amortized to interest expense using the straight-line method over the expected life of the <em style="font: inherit;">2032</em> Notes.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><i style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;"><em style="font: inherit;">2023</em> ABL Facility</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> November 7, 2023, </em>TPB Specialty Finance, LLC, a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company (the &#8220;ABL Borrower&#8221;), entered into a new $<ix:nonFraction id="c145316708" contextRef="i_2023-11-07_DebtInstrumentAxis-AssetBackedRevolvingCreditFacility2023Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">75.0</ix:nonFraction> million&#160;asset-backed revolving credit facility (the <em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2023</em> ABL Facility&#8221;), with the several lenders thereunder, and Barclays Bank Plc, as administrative agent (the &#8220;Administrative Agent&#8221;) and as collateral agent and First-Citizens Bank &amp; Trust Company as additional collateral agent (the &#8220;Additional Collateral Agent&#8221;). Under the <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em> ABL Facility, the ABL Borrower <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>draw up to $<ix:nonFraction id="c145316711" contextRef="i_2023-11-07_DebtInstrumentAxis-AssetBackedRevolvingCreditFacility2023Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">75.0</ix:nonFraction> million under Revolving Credit Loans and Last In Last Out (&#8220;LILO&#8221;) loans. The <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em> ABL Facility includes a $<ix:nonFraction id="c145316713" contextRef="i_2023-11-07_DebtInstrumentAxis-AssetBackedRevolvingCreditFacility2023Member" unitRef="USD" name="tpb:LineOfCreditFacilityAccordionFeature" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">40.0</ix:nonFraction> million accordion feature.&#160;In connection with the <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em> ABL Facility, Turning Point Brands contributed certain existing inventory to the ABL Borrower. The <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em> ABL Facility is secured on a <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> priority basis (subject to customary exceptions) by all assets of the ABL Borrower.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;">The <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em> ABL Facility contains customary borrowing conditions including a borrowing base equal to the sum of (a) the lesser of (<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>) <ix:nonFraction id="c145316719" contextRef="d_2023-11-07_2023-11-07_DebtInstrumentAxis-AssetBackedRevolvingCreditFacility2023Member" unitRef="Pure" name="tpb:DebtInstrumentPercentageUsedInCalculationOfBorrowingBase" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">85</ix:nonFraction>% of the lower of (A) the market value (on a <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> in <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> out basis) of the sum of eligible inventory, plus eligible in-transit inventory of the ABL Borrower and (B) <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145316722">85%</span> of the cost of the sum of eligible inventory, plus eligible in-transit inventory of the ABL Borrower and (<em style="font: inherit;">2</em>) <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145316724">85%</span> of the net orderly liquidation value (&#8220;NOLV&#8221;) percentage of the lower of (<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>)(A) or (<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>)(B); plus (b) <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145316727">85%</span> of the face value of all eligible accounts of the ABL Borrower minus (c) the amount of all eligible reserves.&#160; The <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em> ABL Facility also includes a LILO borrowing base equal to the sum of (a) the lesser of: (<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>) <ix:nonFraction id="c145316730" contextRef="d_2023-11-07_2023-11-07_DebtInstrumentAxis-AssetBackedRevolvingCreditFacility2023Member" unitRef="Pure" name="tpb:DebtInstrumentPercentageUsedInCalculationOfLiloBorrowingBase" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">10</ix:nonFraction>% of the lower of (A) the market value (on a <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> in <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> out basis) of the sum of eligible inventory, plus eligible in-transit inventory of the ABL Borrower and (B) the cost of the sum of eligible inventory, plus eligible in-transit inventory and (<em style="font: inherit;">2</em>) <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145316734">10%</span> of the NOLV percentage of the lower of&#160;(<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>)(A) or (<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>)(B); plus (b) <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145316737">10%</span> of the face amount of eligible account; minus (c) the amount of all eligible reserves.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;">Amounts borrowed under the <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em> ABL Facility are subject to an interest rate margin per annum equal to (a) from and after the closing date until the last day of the <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> full fiscal quarter ended after the closing date, (i) <ix:nonFraction id="c145316740" contextRef="d_2023-11-07_2023-11-07_DebtInstrumentAxis-AssetBackedRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_VariableRateAxis-BaseRateMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentBasisSpreadOnVariableRate1" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">1.25</ix:nonFraction>% per annum, in the case base rate loans, and (ii) <ix:nonFraction id="c145316741" contextRef="d_2023-11-07_2023-11-07_DebtInstrumentAxis-AssetBackedRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_VariableRateAxis-SecuredOvernightFinancingRateSofrMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentBasisSpreadOnVariableRate1" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">2.25</ix:nonFraction>% per annum, in the case of revolving credit loans that are secured overnight financing rate (&#8220;SOFR&#8221;) loans, (b)(i) <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145316742">2.25%</span> per annum, in the case of LILO loans that are base rate loans, and (ii) <ix:nonFraction    <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">10.</em> Income Taxes</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company&#8217;s effective income tax rate for the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2025&#160;</em>was&#160;-<ix:nonFraction id="c145316814" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateContinuingOperations" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3" sign="-">25.2</ix:nonFraction>%&#160;and <ix:nonFraction id="c145316815" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateContinuingOperations" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">11.4</ix:nonFraction>%, respectively. The effective tax rate for the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em> includes permanent tax differences related to the Company's restricted stock units that were issued in the <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> quarter of <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em>&#160;and stock options that were exercised during the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em>&#160;months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">During the <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> quarter of <em style="font: inherit;">2026,</em> the Company concluded that it was more&#8209;likely&#8209;than&#8209;not that TPBI&#8217;s separate company state net operating losses and other deferred tax assets, excluding the State <em style="font: inherit;">&#167;163</em>(j) interest limitation carryforward, would be realizable. As a result, the Company released <em style="font: inherit;">$2.4</em> million of the related valuation allowance as a discrete item in the quarter.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">11.</em> Share Incentive Plans</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 22, 2021,&#160;</em>the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors adopted the Turning Point Brands, Inc.&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2021</em>&#160;Equity Incentive Plan (the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2021</em>&#160;Plan&#8221;), pursuant to which awards&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may&#160;</em>be granted to employees, non-employee directors, and consultants. In addition, the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2021</em>&#160;Plan provides for the granting of nonqualified stock options to employees of the Company or any subsidiary of the Company. Pursuant to the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2021</em>&#160;Plan,&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c145316843" contextRef="i_2021-03-22_PlanNameAxis-TurningPointBrandsInc2021EquityIncentivePlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,290,000</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares, plus&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c145316844" contextRef="i_2021-03-22_PlanNameAxis-TurningPointBrandsInc2015EquityIncentivePlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">100,052</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares remaining available for issuance under the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2015</em>&#160;Equity Incentive Plan (the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2015</em>&#160;Plan&#8221;), of TPB Common Stock are reserved for issuance as awards to employees, non-employee directors, and consultants as compensation for past or future services or the attainment of certain performance goals. The&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2021</em>&#160;Plan is scheduled to terminate on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 21, 2031.&#160;</em>The&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2021</em>&#160;Plan is administered by the compensation committee (the &#8220;Committee&#8221;) of the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors. The Committee determines the vesting criteria for the awards, with such criteria to be specified in the award agreement. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, net of forfeitures, there were <ix:nonFraction id="c145316849" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_PlanNameAxis-TurningPointBrandsInc2021EquityIncentivePlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="tpb:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardAwardsGrantedNetOfForfeituresNumber" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">506,294</ix:nonFraction>&#160;Restricted Stock Units (&#8220;RSUs&#8221;),&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c145316850" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_AwardTypeAxis-EmployeeStockOptionMember_PlanNameAxis-TurningPointBrandsInc2021EquityIncentivePlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="tpb:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardAwardsGrantedNetOfForfeituresNumber" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">122,570</ix:nonFraction>&#160;options and <ix:nonFraction id="c145316851" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_AwardTypeAxis-PerformanceBasedRestrictedStockUnitsMember_PlanNameAxis-TurningPointBrandsInc2021EquityIncentivePlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="tpb:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardAwardsGrantedNetOfForfeituresNumber" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">168,281</ix:nonFraction>&#160;Performance Based Restricted Stock Units (&#8220;PRSUs&#8221;) granted under the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2021</em>&#160;Plan. There are <ix:nonFraction id="c145316853" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_PlanNameAxis-TurningPointBrandsInc2021EquityIncentivePlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAvailableForGrant" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">592,907</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares available for future grant under the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2021</em>&#160;Plan as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> April 28, 2016,&#160;</em>the Board of Directors of the Company adopted the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2015</em>&#160;Plan, pursuant to which awards could have been granted to employees, non-employee directors, and consultants. In addition, the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2015</em>&#160;Plan provided for the granting of nonqualified stock options to employees of the Company or any subsidiary of the Company. Upon adoption of the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2021</em>&#160;Plan, the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2015</em>&#160;Plan was terminated, and the Company determined&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">no</em>&#160;additional grants would be made under the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2015</em>&#160;Plan. However, all awards issued under the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2015</em>&#160;Plan that have&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;been previously terminated or forfeited remain outstanding and continue unaffected.    <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Under the <em style="font: inherit;">2015</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> Plans, the total intrinsic value of options exercised during the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, was&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c145316872" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsExercisesInPeriodTotalIntrinsicValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c145316873" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsExercisesInPeriodTotalIntrinsicValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">At <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, under the <em style="font: inherit;">2015</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> Plans, the risk-free interest rate is based on the U.S. Treasury rate for the expected life at the time of grant. The expected volatility is based on the average long-term historical volatilities of peer companies. We intend to continue to consistently use the same group of publicly traded peer companies to determine expected volatility until sufficient information regarding volatility of our share price becomes available or until the selected companies are <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> longer suitable for this purpose. Due to our limited trading history, we are using the simplified method presented by SEC Staff Accounting Bulletin <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">107</em> to calculate expected holding periods, which represent the periods of time for which options granted are expected to be outstanding. We will continue to use this method until we have sufficient historical exercise experience to give us confidence in the reliability of our calculations. The fair values of these options were determined using the Black-Scholes option pricing model.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <ix:exclude>&#160;</ix:exclude>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">PRSUs are restricted stock units subject to both performance-based and service-based vesting conditions. The number of shares of TPB Common Stock a recipient will receive upon vesting of a PRSU will be calculated by reference to certain performance metrics related to the Company&#8217;s performance over a <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145316888">five</span>-year period. PRSUs will vest on the measurement date, which is <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> more than <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_AwardTypeAxis-PerformanceBasedRestrictedStockUnitsMember" name="tpb:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardPeriodBetweenPerformancePeriodAndMeasurementDate" id="c145316891" format="ixt-sec:duryear">65</ix:nonNumeric> days after the performance period provided the applicable service and performance conditions are satisfied. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, there are <ix:nonFraction id="c145316892" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_AwardTypeAxis-PerformanceBasedRestrictedStockUnitsMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsNonvestedNumber" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">177,725</ix:nonFraction>&#160;PRSUs outstanding. The following table outlines the PRSUs granted and outstanding as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">12.</em>&#160;Contingencies&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Other major tobacco companies are defendants in product liability claims. In a number of these cases, the amounts of punitive and compensatory damages sought are significant and, if such a claim were brought against the Company, could have a material adverse effect on our business and results of operations.&#160;The potential losses associated with any such lawsuits are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> currently reasonably estimable and therefore are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> accrued.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">14.</em> Segment Information</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In accordance with ASC&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">280,</em>&#160;Segment Reporting, the Company has&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145317248">two</span>&#160;reportable segments, Zig-Zag products and Stoker&#8217;s products. The Zig-Zag products segment markets and distributes (i) rolling papers, tubes, and related products; (ii) finished cigars and MYO cigar wraps; and (iii) lighters and other accessories. The Stoker&#8217;s products segment (i) manufactures and markets moist snuff, (ii) contracts for and markets loose-leaf chewing tobacco products, and (iii) contracts for and markets its modern oral product.&#160;The Company's products are distributed primarily through wholesale distributors in the U.S. and Canada.&#160;Corporate unallocated includes the costs and assets of the Company&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;assigned to&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">one</em>&#160;of the&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145317251">two</span>&#160;reportable segments and includes corporate overhead expense, including executive management, finance, legal and information technology salaries, and professional services&#160;such as audit, external legal costs and information technology services, as well as costs related to the FDA premarket tobacco product application.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company&#8217;s CODM is its President and Chief Executive Officer&#160;and uses segment operating income as the measure of earnings to evaluate the performance of each segment and to make decisions about allocating&#160;resources, including employees, property, plant&#160;and&#160;equipment, as well as financial and capital resources.&#160;On a quarterly basis, the CODM reviews segment operating income budget-to-actual variances to assess segment performance and make resource allocation decisions. For both reportable&#160;segments, cost of sales is the significant segment expense that is regularly provided to the CODM.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The accounting policies of these segments are the same as those of the Company. Corporate costs are&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145317252">not</span>&#160;directly charged to the&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145317253">two</span>&#160;reportable segments in the ordinary course of operations.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">The tables below present financial information about reportable segments:</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">A dividend of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145317365" contextRef="d_2025-10-10_2025-10-10_DividendsAxis-O2025Q3DividendsMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:CommonStockDividendsPerShareCashPaid" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">0.08</ix:nonFraction> per common share was paid on <em style="font: inherit;"> April 1, 2026,&#160;</em>to shareholders of record at the close of business on <em style="font: inherit;"> March 20, 2026.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company currently pays a quarterly cash dividend. Dividends are considered restricted payments under the <em style="font: inherit;">2032</em> Notes Indenture. The Company is generally permitted to make restricted payments provided that, at the time of payment, or as a result of payment, the Company is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> in default on its debt covenants; however, there are earnings and market capitalization requirements that if <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> met could limit the aggregate amount of restricted, quarterly dividends during a fiscal year.</p>
