  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>The following Management</i>&#8217;<i>s Discussion and Analysis (</i>&#8220;<i>MD&amp;A</i>&#8221;<i>) relates to the unaudited financial statements of Turning Point Brands, Inc., included elsewhere in this Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q. The MD&amp;A is intended to enable the reader to understand the Company</i>&#8217;<i>s financial condition and results of operations, including any material changes in the Company</i>&#8217;<i>s financial condition and results of operations since December 31, 2025, and as compared with the </i>three months ended March 31, 2025<i>.</i>&#160;<i>The MD&amp;A is provided as a supplement to and should be read in conjunction with the unaudited consolidated financial statements and notes thereto included in this Quarterly report on Form 10-Q, as well as </i>&#8220;<i>Management</i>&#8217;<i>s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations</i>&#8221;<i> contained in the Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended&#160;December 31, 2025 (the </i>&#8220;<i>2025 Annual Report</i>&#8221;<i>).</i></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>In this MD&amp;A, unless the context requires otherwise, references to </i>&#8220;<i>our Company</i>&#8221;<i> </i>&#8220;<i>we,</i>&#8221;<i> </i>&#8220;<i>our,</i>&#8221;<i> or </i>&#8220;<i>us</i>&#8221;<i> refer to Turning Point Brands, Inc., and its consolidated subsidiaries. References to </i>&#8220;<i>TPB</i>&#8221;<i> refer to Turning Point Brands, Inc., without any of its subsidiaries. Many of the amounts and percentages in this discussion have been rounded for convenience of presentation.</i></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Overview</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">Turning Point Brands, Inc. is a leading manufacturer, marketer and distributor of branded consumer products. We sell a wide range of products to adult consumers consisting of staple products with our iconic brands Zig-Zag&#174; and Stoker&#8217;s&#174; and our next-generation products to fulfill evolving consumer preferences. Among other markets, we compete in the alternative smoking accessories and Other Tobacco Products (&#8220;OTP&#8221;) industries. The alternative smoking accessories market is a dynamic market experiencing robust secular growth driven by cannabinoid legalization in the U.S. and Canada and positively evolving consumer perception and acceptance in North America. The OTP industry, which consists of non-cigarette tobacco products, exhibited flat consumer unit annualized growth during the full year period ended 2025 as reported by MSAi a third-party analytics and information company. Our segments are led by our core proprietary and iconic brands: Zig-Zag&#174; in the Zig-Zag products segment and Stoker&#8217;s&#174; along with FRE&#174;, Beech-Nut&#174; and Trophy&#174; in the Stoker&#8217;s products segment. Our businesses generate solid cash flow which we use to invest in our business, finance acquisitions, increase brand support, expand our distribution infrastructure, and strengthen our capital position. We currently ship to approximately 900 distributors with an additional approximately 600 secondary, indirect wholesalers in the U.S. that carry and sell our products. Under the leadership of a senior management team with extensive experience in the consumer products, alternative smoking accessories and tobacco industries, we have grown and diversified our business through new product launches, category expansions and acquisitions while concurrently improving operational efficiency.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">We believe there are meaningful opportunities to expand through investing in organic growth via acquisitions and joint ventures across all product categories. Our products are currently available in approximately 220,000 retail locations in North America. Our sales team targets widespread distribution to all traditional retail channels, including convenience stores, and we have a growing e-commerce business.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Recent Developments</i></p>
  <p style="text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -3px; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;;">&#160;</p>
  <div style="font-size:10pt">
   <div style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;">
    <div style="font-variant:normal">
      On February 20, 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court issued a ruling regarding tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (&#8220;IEEPA&#8221;) on goods imported into the United States, concluding that such tariffs were unauthorized. As of the date of this report, the Company has paid approximately $17.9 million in tariffs subject to the ruling.
    </div>
   </div>
  </div>
  <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <div style="font-size:10pt">
   <div style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;">
    <div style="font-variant:normal">
      The ruling did not address the availability, timing, or amount of any potential refunds.&#160;The U.S. Court of International Trade (&#8220;CIT&#8221;) has ordered the U.S. Customs and Border Protection (&#8220;CBP&#8221;) to refund the collected IEEPA tariffs. The administrative process for seeking refunds of IEEPA tariffs previously paid remains under development and the CIT&#8217;s order may be subject to U.S. government challenge. On April 20, 2026, the CBP launched the Consolidated Administration and Processing of Entries (CAPE) system for IEEPA refunds, which the CBP plans to implement through a phased development approach. There can be no guarantee that a refund, if received, will equal the full amount of IEEPA tariffs paid, and any refund may be subject to taxes and other adjustments or further legal, regulatory, or administration developments. Given these uncertainties, the Company has not recognized any benefit or asset related to potential IEEPA tariff refunds as of this filing date. Following the U.S. Supreme Court's decision, the U.S. administration announced additional tariffs under Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 and could take action to implement additional tariffs in the future. Accordingly, any recovery of amounts paid remains uncertain, and management has concluded that recognition of a receivable or recovery asset is not appropriate at this time.
    </div>
   </div>
  </div>
  <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <div style="font-size:10pt">
   <div style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;">
    <div style="font-variant:normal">
      The Company continues to monitor developments related to this ruling, as well as changes in U.S. and foreign trade, import, and export policies, which could have a material impact on the Company&#8217;s financial position, results of operations, and cash flows.
    </div>
   </div>
  </div>
  <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>Products</i></p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">We operate in two segments: Zig-Zag products and Stoker&#8217;s products segments. In our Zig-Zag products segment, we principally market and distribute (i) rolling papers, tubes&#160;and related products; (ii) finished cigars and make-your-own (&#8220;MYO&#8221;) cigar wraps; and (iii) lighters and other accessories.&#160;In addition, we have a majority stake in Turning Point Brands Canada which is a specialty marketing and distribution firm focused on building brands in the Canadian cannabis accessories, tobacco and alternative products categories. In our Stoker&#8217;s products segment, we (i) manufacture and market moist snuff tobacco (&#8220;MST&#8221;);&#160;(ii) contract for and market&#160;modern oral products; and (iii) contract for and market loose-leaf chewing tobacco products.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>Operations</i></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Our Zig-Zag products and Stoker&#8217;s products segments primarily generate revenues from the sale of our products to wholesale distributors who, in turn, resell the products to retail operations.&#160;Our net sales, which include federal excise taxes, consist of gross sales net of cash discounts, returns, and selling and marketing allowances.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">We rely on long-standing relationships with high-quality, established manufacturers to provide the majority of our produced products. Approximately 75% of our production, as measured by net sales, is outsourced to suppliers. The remaining production consists primarily of our moist snuff tobacco operations located in Dresden, Tennessee and Louisville, Kentucky. Our principal operating expenses include the cost of raw materials used to manufacture the limited number of our products which we produce in-house; the cost of finished products, which are generally purchased goods; federal excise taxes; legal expenses; and compensation expenses, including benefits and costs of salaried personnel.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>Comparison of the Three Months Ended March 31, 2026, to the Three Months Ended March 31, 2025</i></p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Net Sales:</b> For the three months ended March 31, 2026, consolidated net sales increased&#160;$17.8&#160;million, or 16.8%&#160;compared to the prior year period, driven primarily by an increase in the&#160;Stoker&#8217;s products segment.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">For the three months ended March 31, 2026, net sales in the Zig-Zag products segment decreased&#160;$10.6&#160;million, or 22.4%&#160;compared to the prior year period. The decrease&#160;in net sales was driven primarily by declines of $7.4&#160;million in U.S. papers and wraps,&#160;$1.7&#160;million in the Clipper lighter business, and $0.9 million&#160; in our Canadian products.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">For the three months ended March 31, 2026, net sales in the Stoker&#8217;s products segment increased&#160;$28.4&#160;million, or 48.1%&#160;compared to the prior year period. The increase in net sales was primarily driven by $29.7 million of growth in modern oral products.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Gross Profit:</b>&#160;For the three months ended March 31, 2026, consolidated gross profit increased&#160;$8.7&#160;million, or 14.6%&#160;compared to the prior year period. Gross profit as a percentage of net sales decreased&#160;to 55.0% for the three months ended March 31, 2026, compared to&#160;56.0%&#160;for the three months ended March 31, 2025. The overall increase in gross profit was driven by increases in net sales in the Stoker's products segment and driven by margin contribution from modern oral products.&#160;&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">For the three months ended March 31, 2026, gross profit in the Zig-Zag products segment decreased $4.6&#160;million, or 18.1% compared to the prior year period.&#160;Gross profit as a percentage of net sales increased&#160;to 57.1% of net sales for the three months ended March 31, 2026, from 54.1% of net sales for the three months ended March 31, 2025, driven primarily by product mix.&#160;&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">For the three months ended March 31, 2026, gross profit in the Stoker&#8217;s products segment increased&#160;$13.3&#160;million, or 39.1%&#160;compared to the prior year period. Gross profit as a percentage of net sales decreased&#160;to 54.0% of net sales for the three months ended March 31, 2026, from 57.5% of net sales for the three months ended March 31, 2025, primarily driven by margin contribution from modern oral products.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Selling, General, and Administrative Expenses:</b>&#160;For the three months ended March 31, 2026, selling, general, and administrative expenses increased&#160;$19.4&#160;million, or 53.2%&#160;compared to the prior year period, primarily due to increased shipping and selling costs related to the increase&#160;in modern oral sales in the quarter compared to the prior year period. Selling, general and administrative expenses in the three months ended March 31, 2026, included $0.3&#160;million of expense related to PMTA, $2.9&#160;million of stock options, restricted stock and incentives expense,&#160;$0.2&#160;million of legal expenses incurred in connection with litigation related to an insurance claim, and $0.1 million of expense related to corporate restructuring.&#160;Selling, general and administrative expenses in the three months ended March 31, 2025, included $1.7&#160;million of stock options, restricted stock and incentives expense, $1.6&#160;million of expense related to PMTA, $0.2&#160;million of transaction costs, and $0.2&#160;million of expense related to the implementation of the new ERP and CRM systems.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Operating Income:</b>&#160;For the three months ended March 31, 2026, consolidated operating income decreased&#160;$10.7&#160;million, or 46.2%&#160;compared to the prior year period. Operating income as a percentage of net sales decreased&#160;to 10.0% of net sales for the three months ended March 31, 2026 from 21.8% of net sales for the three months ended March 31, 2025, primarily driven by increased&#160;selling, general and administrative costs.&#160;&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">For the three months ended March 31, 2026, operating income in the Zig-Zag products segment decreased&#160;$5.7&#160;million, or 33.7%&#160;compared to the prior year period. Operating income as a percentage of net sales decreased&#160;to 30.6% of net sales for the three months ended March 31, 2026 from 35.8% of net sales for the three months ended March 31, 2025, primarily driven by improved margins on product mix offset by an increase in sales and marketing costs.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">For the three months ended March 31, 2026, operating income in the Stoker&#8217;s products segment decreased&#160;$4.4&#160;million, or 18.1%&#160;compared to the prior year period. Operating income as a percentage of net sales decreased&#160;to 22.6%&#160;of net sales for the three months ended March 31, 2026 from 40.8%&#160;of net sales for the three months ended March 31, 2025, primarily driven by margin contribution of modern oral products and higher sales and marketing costs to drive sales.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Included in consolidated operating income are costs of the Company which are not assigned to one of the two&#160;reportable segments and include: (i) corporate overhead expense, including executive management, finance, legal and information technology salaries, and professional services, such as audit, external legal costs and information technology services, as well as (ii) costs related to the FDA premarket tobacco product application. For the three months ended March 31, 2026, unallocated costs were $18.5 million compared to $17.9 million in the prior year period, an increase of&#160;$0.6&#160;million or 3.6%, primarily driven by joint venture related corporate expenses. &#160;&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Other Expense, net:&#160;</b>For the three months ended March 31, 2026, other&#160;income increased&#160;$0.1&#160;million compared to the prior year period due to an honorarium gift in the current year period that was not applicable in the prior year period.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Interest Expense, net:</b>&#160;For the three months ended March 31, 2026, interest expense, net was $4.4 million, consistent with the prior year period. The level of interest expense remained stable due to no significant changes in average borrowings, interest rates or debt structure during the period.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Investment Gain:</b>&#160;For the three months ended March 31, 2026, investment gain was $0.2&#160;million, consistent with the prior year period. The year-over-year stability reflects comparable investment performance&#160;and an unchanged investment portfolio composition during the period.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Income From Equity Method Investments:</b> For the&#160;three months ended March 31, 2026, income from investments in equity securities increased $2.8 million&#160;compared to the prior year period as a result of GWO.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Loss on Extinguishment of Debt:&#160;</b>There was no loss on extinguishment of debt for the three months ended March 31, 2026. Loss on extinguishment of debt for the three months ended March 31, 2025 was $1.2 million as a result of the redemption of the 2026 Notes in February 2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Income Tax (Benefit) Expense:</b><b>&#160;</b>Our income tax benefit of $2.8 million was (25.2%of income before income taxes for the three months ended March 31, 2026. Our effective income tax rate was 11.4%&#160;for the three months ended March 31, 2025.&#160;The change in tax rate is primarily attributable to the release of a valuation allowance on deferred tax assets.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Net Income Attributable to Non-Controlling Interest:</b><b>&#160;</b>Net income attributable to non-controlling interest was $2.3 million and $1.4&#160;million, respectively,&#160;for the three&#160;months ended March 31, 2026 and 2025.&#160;The increase in non-controlling interest compared to the prior year period is primarily due to higher sales volumes and improved net income.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Net Income Attributable to Turning Point Brands, Inc.:</b>&#160;Due to the factors described above, net income attributable to Turning Point Brands, Inc. for the three&#160;months ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, was $11.7 million and $14.4 million, respectively.</p>

  <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt;"><b>EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">To supplement our financial information presented in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States, or U.S. GAAP, we use non-U.S. GAAP financial measures including EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA. We believe Adjusted EBITDA provides useful information to management and investors regarding certain financial and business trends relating to our financial condition and results of operations. Adjusted EBITDA is used by management to compare our performance to that of prior periods for trend analyses and planning purposes and is presented to our Board of Directors. We believe that EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA are appropriate measures of operating performance because they eliminate the impact of expenses that do not relate to operating performance. In addition, our debt instruments contain covenants which use Adjusted EBITDA calculations.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We define &#8220;EBITDA&#8221; as net income attributable to Turning Point Brands, Inc. before interest expense, gain (loss) on extinguishment of debt, income tax expense, depreciation&#160;and amortization. We define &#8220;Adjusted EBITDA&#8221; as net income before interest expense, gain (loss) on extinguishment of debt, income tax expense, depreciation, amortization, other non-cash items&#160;and other items we do not consider the ordinary course in our evaluation of ongoing operating performance noted in the reconciliation below. Among other items that we adjust Adjusted EBITDA for is FDA PMTA expense. The Company believes it is appropriate to adjust for this spend as the costs are incurred in connection with what we view as a non-traditional regulatory process that requires applications be submitted for covered products that are already on the market. As a result, Company&#8217;s management believes it is most appropriate to assess the performance of the Company&#8217;s business &#8211; the sale of our various products - without regard to these costs and believes that adjusting for these costs provides investors and the public markets with the most meaningful metrics to assess performance of the business. The Company reconciles its EBITDA metrics to Net income attributable to Turning Point Brands, Inc. because&#160;that measure reflects the Company&#8217;s portion of the profitability from consolidated joint ventures after removing results attributable to our partners in such joint ventures.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Non-U.S. GAAP measures should not be considered a substitute for, or superior to, financial measures calculated in accordance with U.S. GAAP. Adjusted EBITDA excludes significant expenses required to be recorded in our financial statements by U.S. GAAP and is subject to inherent limitations. Other companies in our industry may calculate this non-U.S. GAAP measure differently than we do or may not calculate it at all, limiting its usefulness as a comparative measure. The tables below provide reconciliations between net income and Adjusted EBITDA.</p>

The application is a one-time resource-intensive process for each covered product line; however, due to the nature of the implementation process for those product lines already in the market, applications can take multiple years to complete rather than the typical one-time submission. The Company has only two product lines currently subject to the PMTA process, having utilized other regulatory pathway options available for our other product lines. The Company does not expect to submit additional PMTA applications for any new product lines after the submission for the remaining two are complete.</p> </td>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Liquidity and Capital Resources</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">As of March 31, 2026, we have $192.4&#160;million of cash on hand and $72.6&#160;million of availability under the 2023 ABL Facility. We have no borrowings outstanding under our 2023 ABL Facility as of March 31, 2026. Our principal uses for cash are working capital, debt service, and capital expenditures.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Our adjusted working capital,&#160;which we define as current assets less cash and current liabilities, increased $35.1&#160;million compared to the prior year end. The increase in working capital&#160;is primarily the&#160;result of a $1.7&#160;million increase in accounts receivable, an $21.6 million increase in inventory and a $8.0 million increase in other current assets,&#160;partially offset by an&#160;increase of $15.5&#160;million in accounts payable and a $19.2 million decrease in accrued liabilities.&#160;With our strong cash balance, free cash flow generation and borrowing availability under the 2023 ABL Facility, we expect to have ample liquidity to satisfy our operating cash requirements for the foreseeable future.</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Cash Flows from Operating Activities</i></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">For the three months ended March 31, 2026, net cash used in operating activities was $22.3&#160;million, a increase&#160;of $39.7&#160;million compared to the prior year period. The increase&#160;is primarily due to unfavorable&#160;changes of $34.5&#160;million in working capital,&#160;&#160;$1.2&#160;million in other assets, decrease&#160;in net income, net of non-cash items of $6.3&#160;million.&#160;The primary drivers of non-cash items were a $1.6&#160;million increase&#160;in deferred tax benefit, a $0.4&#160;million increase&#160;in depreciation and amortization,&#160; a $2.8 million increase in income from equity method investment&#160;and a $1.2 million decrease in loss on extinguishment of debt compared to the prior year period.&#160;The decrease in cash from working capital compared to the prior year period was primarily driven by the timing of payments.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Cash Flows from Investing Activities</i></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">For the three months ended March 31, 2026, net cash used in&#160;investing activities was $5.1&#160;million, a&#160;decrease&#160;of $0.2&#160;million compared to the prior year period, primarily due to an increase&#160;in capital expenditures of $3.0&#160;million offset by&#160;$2.8 million decrease for investments.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Cash Flows from Financing Activities</i></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">For the three months ended March 31, 2026, net cash used in&#160;financing activities was $2.7&#160;million, a decrease&#160;of $41.2&#160;million compared to the prior year period,&#160;primarily due to a net decrease&#160;in cash of $43.4&#160;million related to the February 2025 issuance of the 2032&#160;Notes, and $2.5&#160;million related to stock compensation activity.</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Dividends, Share Issuances,&#160;and Shares Repurchases</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">A dividend of&#160;&#160;$0.08&#160;per common share was paid on April 10, 2026,&#160;to shareholders of record at the close of business on March 20, 2026.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">On February 25, 2020, our Board of Directors approved a $50.0 million share repurchase program, which is intended for opportunistic execution based upon a variety of factors including market dynamics. The program is subject to the ongoing discretion of the Board of Directors. On October 25, 2021, the Board of Directors increased the approved share repurchase program by $30.7 million, and by $24.6 million on February 24, 2022. On November 6, 2024, the Company's Board of Directors increased the Company&#8217;s share repurchase authorization by $77.9 million to an aggregate amount of $100.0 million. On November 4,&#160;2025,&#160;the Company's Board of Directors increased the share repurchase authorization by $100.0&#160;million to an aggregate amount of $200.0&#160;million. For&#160;the&#160;three months ended March 31, 2026, there were no repurchases under the share repurchase program. As of March 31, 2026, there was $200.0 million in remaining repurchase authority under the plan.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">The Company entered into an at-the-market offering program (the "ATM Program") on&#160;December 13, 2024,&#160;with B. Riley Securities Inc. and Barclays Capital Inc. Between&#160;August 15, 2025,&#160;and&#160;September 11, 2025,&#160;the Company sold&#160;1,014,262&#160;shares of our Common Stock under the ATM Program at an average selling price of $98.59&#160;per share for gross proceeds of $100.0&#160;million, less underwriter's commission and expenses of approximately $2.5&#160;million, for net proceeds of $97.5&#160;million. The shares were issued from repurchased common stock on a&#160;first&#160;in&#160;first&#160;out basis. The Company recorded the gain, corresponding to the difference in between the reacquisition cost of treasury stock and the value of treasury stock reissued, into APIC within the Consolidated Statements of Changes in Stockholders' Equity. As of&#160;March 31, 2026,&#160;there was $200.0 million of capacity remaining under the ATM Program.</p>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>2032 Notes</i></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In February 2025, the Company&#160;closed a private offering of $300.0&#160;million aggregate principal amount of 7.625% senior secured notes due to mature on March 15, 2032 (the &#8220;2032 Notes&#8221;). Interest on the 2032 Notes is payable semi-annually on March 15 and September 15 of each year, commencing on September 15, 2025. We used the proceeds from the offering (i) to repay all obligations under and redeem all of our 5.625% senior secured notes due 2026 (the "2026 Notes), (ii) to pay related fees, costs&#160;and expenses and (iii) for general corporate purposes.&#160;The 2032 Notes are fully and unconditionally guaranteed on a senior secured basis, jointly and severally, by each current and future wholly-owned domestic restricted subsidiary of the Company that guaranteed the 2026 Notes (collectively, the &#8220;Guarantors&#8221; as defined in the indenture governing the 2032 Notes or the &#8220;2032 Notes Indenture&#8221;).&#160;The 2032 Notes and the related guarantees are secured by first-priority liens on substantially all of the assets of the&#160;Company and the Guarantors, subject to certain exceptions. Proceeds from the offering were approximately $293.0 million.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The 2032 Notes Indenture contains covenants that, among other things, restrict the ability of the Company and its restricted subsidiaries to: (i) grant or incur liens; (ii) incur, assume or guarantee additional indebtedness; (iii) sell or otherwise dispose of assets, including capital stock of subsidiaries; (iv) make certain investments; (v) pay dividends, make distributions or redeem or repurchase capital stock; (vi) engage in certain transactions with affiliates; and (vii) consolidate or merge with or into, or sell substantially all of our assets to another entity. These covenants are subject to several limitations and exceptions set forth in the 2032 Notes Indenture. For instance, the Company is generally permitted to make restricted payments, including the payment of dividends to shareholders, provided that, at the time of payment, or as a result of payment, the Company is not in default on its debt covenants; however, there are earnings and market capitalization requirements that if not met could limit the aggregate amount of quarterly dividends payable during a fiscal year. The 2032 Notes Indenture provides for customary events of default.&#160;The Company was in compliance with all covenants under the 2032 Notes as of March 31, 2026.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We incurred debt issuance costs attributable to the 2032&#160;Notes of $7.3&#160;million which are amortized to interest expense using the straight-line method over the expected life of the 2032 Notes.</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>2023 ABL Facility</i></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">On November 7, 2023, TPB Specialty Finance, LLC, a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company (the &#8220;ABL Borrower&#8221;), entered into a new $75.0 million&#160; asset-backed revolving credit facility (the &#8220;2023 ABL Facility&#8221;), with the several lenders thereunder, and Barclays Bank Plc, as administrative agent (the &#8220;Administrative Agent&#8221;) and as collateral agent and First-Citizens Bank &amp; Trust Company as additional collateral agent (the &#8220;Additional Collateral Agent&#8221;). Under the 2023 ABL Facility, the ABL Borrower may draw up to $75.0 million under Revolving Credit Loans and Last In Last Out (&#8220;LILO&#8221;) Loans. The 2023 ABL Facility includes a $40.0 million accordion feature.&#160;In connection with the 2023 ABL Facility, Turning Point Brands contributed certain existing inventory to the ABL Borrower. The 2023 ABL Facility is secured on a first priority basis (subject to customary exceptions) by all assets of the ABL Borrower.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The 2023 ABL Facility contains customary borrowing conditions including a borrowing base equal to the sum of (a) the lesser of (1) 85% of the lower of (A) the market value (on a first in first out basis) of the sum of eligible inventory, plus eligible in-transit inventory of the ABL Borrower and (B) 85% of the cost of the sum of eligible inventory, plus eligible in-transit inventory of the ABL Borrower and (2) 85% of the net orderly liquidation value (&#8220;NOLV&#8221;) percentage of the lower of (1)(A) or (1)(B); plus (b) 85% of the face value of all eligible accounts of the ABL Borrower minus (c) the amount of all eligible reserves.&#160; The 2023 ABL Facility also includes a LILO borrowing base equal to the sum of (a) the lesser of: (1) 10% of the lower of (A) the market value (on a first in first out basis) of the sum of eligible inventory, plus eligible in-transit inventory of the ABL Borrower and (B) the cost of the sum of eligible inventory, plus eligible in-transit inventory and (2) 10% of the NOLV percentage of the lower of&#160;(1)(A) or (1)(B); plus (b) 10% of the face amount of eligible account; minus (c) the amount of all eligible reserves.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Amounts borrowed under the 2023 ABL Facility are subject to an interest rate margin per annum equal to (a) from and after the closing date until the last day of the first full fiscal quarter ended after the closing date, (i) 1.25% per annum, in the case base rate loans, and (ii) 2.25% per annum, in the case of revolving credit loans that are secured overnight financing rate (&#8220;SOFR&#8221;) loans, (b)(i) 2.25% per annum, in the case of LILO loans that are base rate loans, and (ii) 3.25% per annum, in the case of LILO loans that are SOFR loans, (c) on the first day of each fiscal quarter, the applicable interest rate margins will be determined from the pricing grid below based upon the historical excess availability for the most recent fiscal quarter ended immediately prior to the relevant date, as calculated by the Administrative Agent.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The 2023 ABL Facility also requires the Company and its restricted subsidiaries to maintain a fixed charge coverage ratio of at least 1.00 to 1.00 as of the end of any four consecutive fiscal quarters if excess availability is less than the greater of (a) 12.5% of the line cap and (b) $9.4 million, at any time and continuing until excess availability is equal to or exceeds the greater of (i) 12.5% of the line and (ii) $9.4 million for thirty (30) consecutive calendar days with the $9.4 million level automatically increased in proportion to the amount of any increase in the aggregate revolving credit commitments thereunder in connection with any incremental facility.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The 2023 ABL Facility will mature on the earlier of (x) November 7, 2027 and (y) the date that is 91 days prior to the maturity date of any material debt of the ABL Borrower or the Company or any of its restricted subsidiaries (subject to customary extensions agreed by the lenders thereunder); provided that clause (y) will not apply to the extent that on any applicable date of determination (on any date prior to the date set forth in clause (y)), (A) the sum of (x) cash that is held in escrow for the repayment of such material debt pursuant to arrangements satisfactory to the Administrative Agent, (y) cash that is held in accounts with the Administrative Agent and/or the Additional Collateral Agent, plus (z) excess availability, is sufficient to repay such material debt and (B) the ABL Borrower has excess availability of at least $15.0 million after giving effect to such repayment of material debt, including any borrowings under the commitments in connection therewith.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company has not drawn any borrowings under the 2023 ABL Facility but has letters of credit of approximately $2.3 million outstanding under the facility and has an available balance of $72.6&#160;million based on the borrowing base as of March 31, 2026.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company incurred debt issuance costs attributable to the 2023 ABL Facility of $2.6 million which are amortized to interest expense using the straight-line method over the expected life of the 2023 ABL Facility.</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Off-balance Sheet Arrangements</b></p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Inflation</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Inflation&#160;has&#160;a substantial negative effect on the purchasing power of consumers. While historically, we have been able to increase prices at a rate equal to or greater than that of inflation, doing so could be difficult in an inflationary environment. However, we have implemented price increases in areas where doing so has been feasible. In addition, we have been able to maintain a relatively stable variable cost structure for our products due, in part, to our existing contractual agreements for the purchases of tobacco and our premium cigarette rolling papers.</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Foreign Currency Sensitivity</b></p>

Please refer to our &#8216;Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk&#8217; included in our 2025 Annual Report on Form 10-K filed with the SEC.</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">During the three months ended March 31, 2026, there have been no material changes in our exposure to credit risk, as reported within our 2025 Annual Report on Form 10-K.   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Interest Rate Sensitivity</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">In February 2025, we issued the 2032&#160;Notes in an aggregate principal amount of $300.0 million. We carry the 2032&#160;Notes at face value. Since the 2032&#160;Notes bear interest at a fixed rate, we have no financial statement risk associated with changes in interest rates. Our remaining debt instrument is the 2023 ABL Facility, which as of March 31, 2026 and the filing date of this report had&#160;no borrowings outstanding.</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; "><a id="controls" title="controls" href="#"></a>Item 4. Controls and Procedures</span></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">Our management, with the participation of our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting as defined in Rules 13a-15(f) and 15d-15(f) under the Securities Act. Our internal control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of our consolidated financial statements for external reporting purposes in accordance with GAAP. Our internal control over financial reporting includes policies and procedures that: (1) pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of our assets; (2) provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of consolidated financial statements in accordance with GAAP; (3) provide reasonable assurance that our receipts and expenditures are being made only in accordance with authorizations of our management and directors; and (4) provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use or disposition of our assets that could have a material effect on the consolidated financial statements.</p>
  <p style="margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements. Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">Our management, with the participation of our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, conducted an assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2025 based on the 2013 Internal Control &#8212; Integrated Framework (the &#8220;COSO Framework&#8221;) issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations (COSO). Based on this assessment under the COSO Framework, our management has concluded that our internal control over financial reporting was effective as of December 31, 2025.</p>
  <p style="margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Changes in Internal Controls over Financial Reporting</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">There were no&#160;changes in the Company&#8217;s internal controls over financial reporting during the quarter ended March 31, 2026&#160;that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting.</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; "><a id="unregistered" title="unregistered" href="#"></a>Item 2.</span></b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">&#160;</span><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Unregistered Sales of Equity Securities and Use of Proceeds</span></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">On February 25, 2020, the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors approved a $50.0 million share repurchase program, which is intended for opportunistic execution based upon a variety of factors including market dynamics. On October 25, 2021, the Board of Directors increased the approved share repurchase program by $30.7 million, and by an additional $24.6 million on February 24, 2022.&#160;On November 6, 2024, the Company's Board of Directors&#160;increased the&#160;Company&#8217;s&#160;share repurchase&#160;authorization by $77.9 million to an aggregate amount of $100.0 million. On November<span style="background-color:#ffffff;"> 4,</span>&#160;2025,&#160;the Company's Board of Directors increased the share repurchase authorization by $100.0&#160;million to an aggregate amount of $200.0&#160;million. As of March 31, 2026, there remains $200.0 million&#160;in authority to repurchase shares under the plan. This share repurchase program has no expiration date and is subject to the ongoing discretion of the Board of Directors. All repurchases to date under our stock repurchase programs have been made through open market transactions, but in the future, we may also purchase shares through privately negotiated transactions or 10b5-1 repurchase plans.</p>
